web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Twelve Years of Audited Numbers — Margin Bridges, Cash Conversion & the ROE Puzzle
question: What do 10+ years of consolidated P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, and ratio statements reveal about GHFL's earnings quality, cash conversion, and why ROE lags ROCE?

epigraph.quote: Accounting profits can be flattered for a year or two, but twelve consecutive years of positive operating cash flow leave nowhere for bad economics to hide.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.title: 6.1 10-Year P&L Trajectory: Structural Margin Expansion & Interest Elimination

web_blocks.html: Over the twelve years from FY15 through TTM (Sep 2026), GHFL's income statement shows strong operating leverage. Revenue grew from ₹896 Cr in FY15 to ₹2,120 Cr in FY26 and ₹2,384 Cr TTM (+15% TTM growth) [1]. Operating profit jumped more than ninefold—from ₹60 Cr (7% OPM) in FY15 to ₹435 Cr (21% OPM) in FY26 and ₹547 Cr (23% OPM) TTM [1]. Meanwhile, annual interest fell from ₹44 Cr in FY15–FY16 to ₹8 Cr in FY26 as debt was paid off [1]. That helped net profit surge nearly 24-fold from ₹18 Cr (FY15) to ₹338 Cr (FY26) and ₹426 Cr TTM [1]. Effective tax rates also eased from 34–38% (FY15–FY21) down to 24–26% (FY23–FY26) under India's lower corporate tax regime [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY18 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating margins expanded from 10% in FY18 to 21% in FY25–FY26 and 23% TTM, while interest fell from ₹25 Cr to ₹8 Cr [1].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Balance Sheet Forensics: Debt-Free Fortress & The ROE-vs-ROCE Gap

web_blocks.html: GHFL's balance sheet is a fortress: total debt fell from ₹368 Cr in FY15 to ₹0 in FY24–FY26 (with ₹13 Cr in Sep 2026) [1]. Still, a careful reader will spot a puzzle in the return ratios. Why is ROE (13.5%) much lower than ROCE (18.1%) [1]? Two balance-sheet items explain the whole gap. First, in FY17, Reserves jumped from ₹562 Cr to ₹1,231 Cr as Fixed Assets doubled from ₹648 Cr to ₹1,231 Cr [1]. That Ind-AS fair-value reset of land and plant assets permanently raised the book-equity base [1]. Second, GHFL built up ₹698 Cr of Investments by Mar 2026, rising to ₹813 Cr by Sep 2026 [1, 11]. Total cash and equivalents hit ₹933 Cr, earning lower pre-tax treasury yields (~8–9%) than the core film plants [1, 11]. Stripping out treasury cash and revaluation reserves puts core operating capital returns well above 25%.

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY18 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Borrowings fell from ₹171 Cr (FY18) to ₹0 (FY24–FY26) while Investments grew from ₹36 Cr to ₹813 Cr by Sep 2026 [1].

web_blocks.title: 6.3 Cash Conversion, Capex & Working Capital Discipline

web_blocks.html: Across all twelve audited years from FY15 through FY26, GHFL never posted negative Cash from Operations (CFO) [1]. Cumulative CFO over FY21–FY26 reached ₹1,366 Cr versus ₹1,331 Cr of Net Profit (103% CFO/PAT conversion) [1]. Over that same six-year span, Free Cash Flow totaled ₹805 Cr even after funding major PPF and SCF plant expansions [1]. Working capital shifted from negative in FY15–FY17 to positive 28–40 days in FY25–FY26 as overseas stock grew [1]. Note also that the dividend payout ratio fell from 27–28% in FY19–FY20 to 8% in FY25–FY26 as cash piled up [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY17 – FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Twelve consecutive years of positive CFO and Free Cash Flow, with FY25 FCF peaking at ₹276 Cr and FY26 FCF at ₹114 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY17 – FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor Days compressed to 7–9 days, while Inventory Days rose to 149 days in FY26; ROCE climbed from 5% (FY17–FY18) to 18–21% (FY25–FY26) [1].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Earnings Quality Verdict
paragraphs: Cumulative 6-year CFO/PAT of 103%, single-digit Debtor Days (7–9 days), and a debt-free balance sheet confirm that GHFL's margin expansion is backed by real cash collection rather than aggressive accounting [1]. The primary capital-efficiency drag is idle treasury cash and low dividend payout (8% in FY25–FY26) [1].

web_blocks.title: 6.4 Quarterly Momentum Through Sep 2026: Margin & Cash Inflection

web_blocks.html: Quarterly results from Sep 2023 through Sep 2026 show that H1 FY27 marks a lasting step-up in operating leverage [1, 8]. Q3 FY26 dipped to ₹459 Cr in sales and 15% OPM during peak US tariff fears [1, 8]. Then Q4 FY26 bounced back to ₹597 Cr (23% OPM), and Q1 FY27 climbed to ₹633 Cr (27% OPM; 30.3% EBITDA margin with other income) [1, 8, 11]. Q2 FY27 set a record at ₹696 Cr in sales (24% OPM; ₹129 Cr PAT) [1, 8, 11]. With ₹933 Cr of cash on hand as of September 30, 2026, GHFL can fund its TPU and SCF launches from internal cash [11]. Notice how clean the profit-to-cash bridge stays across cycles. Even during the FY26 US tariff pause, operating cash flow reached ₹275 Cr and free cash flow stayed positive at ₹114 Cr [1]. Zero long-term debt also removes interest-rate risk from the income statement [1]. With ₹933 Cr in cash and investments, GHFL can fund its ₹191 Cr solar-film line without raising debt or diluting equity [1, 11, 13].

book_paragraphs: Numbers rarely lie if you read twelve years of them together. When you and I open Garware Hi-Tech Films' consolidated statements from FY15 through September 2026, the first thing that jumps off the page is the sheer durability of cash generation: in twelve consecutive audited fiscal years, Garware never once reported negative operating cash flow.

Let's trace the income statement first. Between FY18 and FY26, revenue more than doubled from ₹833 crore to ₹2,120 crore, and reached ₹2,384 crore on a trailing-twelve-month basis through September 2026. Over that same stretch, core operating profit multiplied more than fivefold from ₹83 crore to ₹435 crore in FY26—and ₹547 crore trailing—lifting operating margins from 10% to 23%. Meanwhile, interest expense shrank from ₹44 crore in FY15 to ₹8 crore in FY26 as management wiped out all long-term debt.

Now look closely at the balance sheet, because there is a subtle forensic puzzle every careful investor should understand. Screener reports an 18.1% ROCE alongside a 13.5% ROE—a gap that makes return on equity look artificially muted. Why? Two reasons. First, back in FY17, an Ind-AS asset revaluation lifted Fixed Assets and Reserves by nearly ₹670 crore overnight, permanently inflating accounting book equity. Second, Garware has accumulated ₹813 crore of treasury investments by September 2026—part of ₹933 crore in total cash and equivalents—earning modest treasury yields that dilute overall ROE. Inside the actual factories, operating capital returns are far healthier than headline ROE suggests.

Finally, check the cash conversion. Over the six years from FY21 through FY26, Garware generated ₹1,366 crore of operating cash flow against ₹1,331 crore of net profit—over 100% cash conversion—and delivered ₹805 crore of free cash flow after funding its PPF and solar-film expansions. Debtor days sit at an enviable 9 days. The only friction on the working-capital line is inventory, which climbed to 149 days in FY26 to support overseas warehouses, alongside a conservative 8% dividend payout ratio. Overall, the financial statements confirm a genuine, self-funded specialty compounder—one whose business quality stands on solid forensic ground before we ever glance at a stock quote.

book_subsections.title: The Six-Year Cash Conversion & Self-Funded Capex Scorecard
paragraphs: If you want one quick sanity check on whether a manufacturer's profits are real, add up six years of net profit and compare it to six years of operating cash flow. From FY21 through FY26, Garware reported ₹1,331 crore in cumulative net profit and generated ₹1,366 crore in cash from operations—a 103% conversion rate.

Even better, after paying for every rupee of new PPF and solar-control expansion capex, the company still generated ₹805 crore in cumulative free cash flow. That is why borrowings fell from ₹182 crore in FY22 to zero by FY24 while investments swelled to ₹813 crore by September 2026. Whatever cyclical bumps occur in quarterly export orders, this is a balance sheet built to survive storms and fund its own growth.

Before we close the blind forensic audit, look at the quarterly cadence through September 2026. After that brief Q3 FY26 air-pocket of ₹459 crore in sales and 15% operating margins, the business snapped back with ₹597 crore in Q4 FY26, ₹633 crore in Q1 FY27, and a record ₹696 crore in Q2 FY27—delivering ₹262 crore of net profit in just the first six months of FY27. With ₹933 crore of cash and equivalents on hand, Garware has earned a clear COMPOUNDER_PASS on underlying business quality, paired with a PASS_WITH_WATCH on KPIs for U.S. tariff exposure, inventory discipline, and capital deployment.

book_callouts.title: Why Accounting ROE Understates Factory Economics
book_callouts.text: The FY17 fixed-asset revaluation reserve (~₹670 Cr) and ₹813 Cr of treasury investments sit in the equity denominator, masking the 25%+ pre-tax returns generated by the core specialty film lines.
